zh.title: Agent 怎样改进自己：改程序、学示范与验证收益
zh.summary: 今天读三篇 2026 年研究，把“自我改进”拆成能追踪的实际操作。主读 AIDE²：一个研究助手修改另一个研究助手的控制程序，哪些改动被留下，换任务后还管不管用？选读 SDFT，理解怎样把示范中的信息学进模型权重；再读 REUSE，解释为什么反复用同一套题选版本，可能把碰巧涨分误认成进步。每篇先讲具体例子，再看机制、实验和限制。只精读主读即可；两篇选读按兴趣展开。

en.title: How agents improve: rewriting code, learning from demonstrations, and checking gains
en.summary: Three 2026 studies turn self-improvement into operations we can trace. The main reading, AIDE², has one research agent rewrite another agent's control program: which changes survive, and do they help on new tasks? SDFT explains how information in demonstrations can enter model weights. REUSE asks why repeatedly selecting versions on one benchmark can mistake lucky gains for progress. Each note starts with a concrete example, then develops the mechanism, evidence, and limitations. Read the main paper closely; explore the two optional papers as interest dictates.

papers.title: Recursive self-improvement of AI research agents

zh.contribution: 让研究 agent 的控制代码也成为实验对象：自动提出改写，让新版本完成一组研究任务，再保留表现更好的版本。论文报告多次连续改进与独立任务上的迁移，同时单独检验“改进后的 agent 是否更善于继续改进自己”。
zh.relevance: 今天的问题已不只是 agent 能否完成一项研究，而是能否改进做研究的方法。它把搜索决策、上下文管理、实验反馈这些可编辑部分连成了可测量的循环，也展示了距离自我加速仍缺什么证据。
zh.reading: 本期主读，建议 35–50 分钟。先理解内层改任务代码、外层改 agent 代码，再读搜索与记忆机制；最后重点看独立测试和 ignition 实验，不要只看上升曲线。
zh.prerequisites: 只需知道一段训练脚本能运行并得到验证分数。正文会解释 agent 控制代码、候选搜索、保留数据和多臂老虎机，不需要强化学习或元学习公式。
zh.caveat: 基础模型权重固定，主实验的外层改写者也固定；7 次接受改写不等于 7 代更强的自改进者。外部收益并不逐代单调，天气验证只有一个任务，让改进版本接手改写的实验尚无显著优势。

sections.heading: 先让 agent 改训练脚本，再问它能否改进做实验的方法
paragraphs: 假设我们交给 agent 一份图像分类训练脚本，希望它在有限预算内提高准确率。它可以改学习率，运行训练，看验证集结果，再决定保留修改还是试另一个办法。这里先改的是解决具体任务的代码。**这个分类任务是贯穿本文的教学例子，不是论文公布的某一道实验题。**
现在把问题往上一层推：为什么它总是在同一个方案上微调？为什么每轮都把全部旧日志塞进输入？能否修改决定下一步实验、保存历史和检查结果的程序，让它今后做不同任务都更有效？模型之外这层组织工作的代码，论文称为 harness，下面叫 agent 控制代码。

AIDE² 来自 Weco AI。团队于 2026 年 7 月 14 日先发博客，9 月 22 日公开论文 v1；本文以论文为准，属于 2026 年预印本。它研究的是持续修改研究工具本身，而不是让模型重写一次答案就宣称学会了自我改进。[论文](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.26457)；[团队早期说明](https://www.weco.ai/blog/first-evidence-of-recursive-self-improvement)

sections.heading: 内外两层循环分别改什么，哪些部分一直固定
paragraphs: 内层收到具体任务，反复修改任务代码。例如在分类任务里，它会产生几份训练脚本，执行后留下分数与错误记录，预算耗尽时选一份提交。外层收到的则是这个研究 agent 的代码，修改它怎样挑实验、组织输入和处理反馈。评估一个外层改动，要让改后的 agent 再做一组内层任务。
主实验由人工开发的 AIDE_human 担任外层改写者，它在整段运行中不变；每次获准保留的，是下一轮继续被修改的内层 agent。两个循环调用的基础模型也固定：外层 Claude Opus 4.7，内层评估 Gemini 3 Flash。没有在这里训练这些语言模型的权重。[原文 §2.1–2.2、Figure 1](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.26457v1)
因此要分清“持续改进同一套研究程序”与“每一代都换一个更强的改写者”。前者是主实验做的事，后者需要额外检验。固定语言模型，也不意味着内层任务不能训练分类模型；限制针对驱动 agent 的基础模型，不是禁止它执行研究任务。

sections.heading: 三层反馈，分别防止什么误判
paragraphs: 回到分类例子：agent 可以反复看到公开验证分数，靠它选择下一次实验。但反复试得足够多，也可能只找到迎合这份验证数据的脚本。因此内层提交最终方案后，还要在它看不到的私有数据上评分。外层把多个任务的私有分数合成一个成绩，用来决定 agent 改写是否保留。[原文 §2.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.26457v1)
这里的“私有”是相对于内层求解者而言。外层会反复利用合成成绩选版本，所以这份成绩仍然参与了开发，不能充当最终泛化证明。还需要第三层：冻结已选中的 agent，再放到从未参与版本选择的新任务上测试。这才区分出“更会应付选拔题”与“研究方法能迁移”。
**以下是解释这三层设计的推导：** 公开反馈回答“下一份任务代码该怎么改”，私有成绩回答“这个 agent 版本值不值得留下”，独立外部测试回答“留下的改动能否帮助新任务”。三者即使都叫 evaluation，也承担不同职责，不能因为数据对某一层隐藏，就把它当作对整个系统从未使用的测试集。

sections.heading: 搜索改进：别把全部预算押在当前第一名上
paragraphs: 起始 agent 偏向继续改分数最高的候选。教学例子中，假设调学习率的方案略胜于改数据预处理，它就可能把后面的尝试都投给前者。但预处理暂时低分，也可能只是还没调好；只追当前第一名，会过早放弃其他方向。相反，每次都从零开新方案，又无法积累已有进展。
最终版本 AIDE85 把起草策略分成五类，先挑策略，再改该策略下表现最好的候选。选择策略时使用多臂老虎机方法：综合过去收益与尚未充分尝试的程度，分配下一次尝试。论文具体使用 UCB1，并混合另一种按分数采样的选择；还周期性地把最好方案交给不同策略继续改。[原文 §3.5、Figure 5](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.26457v1)
这不要求模型凭空发明一项全新的研究方向。它改变的是实验预算怎样分配：已有好代码可以保留，但下一轮尝试的角度可以改变。**对分类例子的类比是我们自己的解释：** 不是丢掉最佳训练脚本，而是让另一条优化思路从这份脚本继续探索。

sections.heading: 记忆改进：保留能影响下一步的记录
paragraphs: 若已做过 30 次实验，把 30 份完整脚本和所有日志一起发送，输入会越来越长。下一次只想修一个导入错误，却仍需处理许多无关的成功实验。删掉全部历史也不行：它可能重复试过的失败办法。这是信息取舍问题，不是输入越长就一定记得越好。
AIDE85 改用较短、按角色组织的输入：提出新方案与改进旧方案时，读取根方案和近期候选的摘要；错误较多时，再加入重复出现的错误记录。它不再像起始版本那样不断拼接完整历史。这是写入控制程序、在后续任务中继续生效的变化。[原文 §3.5、Figure 6](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.26457v1)
**从机制可推导的价值是：** 在按调用与执行费用约束的任务里，减少无用输入可以给更多有效尝试留出预算。但短输入不保证更高成绩，删去关键反例也可能让决策变差。因此最终仍应以整个研究任务的结果判断，而不是把压缩比例直接解释成相同倍数的研究加速。

sections.heading: 八天的上升曲线，实际包含多少次改进
paragraphs: 主运行持续八天，共 100 个节点：一个起始 agent，加 99 次改写提案。其中 7 次获准替换当前最佳版本，合成私有成绩从 0.703 升到 0.778。另两次完整运行分别接受了 2 次和 4 次改写。它提供了重复找到有用修改的证据，但不是每次尝试都成功。[原文 §3.2、Figure 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.26457v1)
0.703 和 0.778 是选拔任务的合成成绩，不能读成“通用研究能力从 70.3% 提升到 77.8%”。被接受的曲线只保留迄今最好版本，本来就不会因淘汰较差候选而下降。真正值得检查的是尝试了多少候选、接受依据是否可靠，以及这些版本在独立任务上怎样表现。
人工仍负责定义起始系统、任务集合、每项预算和保留准则；自动完成的是运行中的提案、执行与比较。团队声明循环内没有人工介入，但这不等于没有人工设计。把八天与团队此前两年的开发经历并列，可以说明背景，不能据此算出在同等条件下替代研究人员的倍数。[团队说明](https://www.weco.ai/blog/first-evidence-of-recursive-self-improvement)

sections.heading: 换一批研究任务，改进是否仍然存在
paragraphs: 作者在未参与选拔的 ALE-Bench、MLE-Bench、FML-Bench 和基于 WeatherBench 2 的天气任务上比较起始、改进中途、最终以及人工开发版本。前三类覆盖算法或机器学习工程，天气任务则考察此前未出现的物理预测程序优化。每个基准内部，各 agent 遵守相同协议。[原文 §3.3、附录 A](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.26457v1)

以机器学习工程为例，MLE-Bench lite 包含 22 项比赛，每项运行三个种子。各 agent 使用 Gemini 3 Flash，每次主要预算为 5 美元，任务脚本在 4–24 vCPU、16–192 GB 内存的 CPU 容器中执行。私有排名分数的均值从 AIDE0 的 0.678±0.006，升到 AIDE85 的 0.722±0.011；人工版本为 0.708±0.007。± 表示一个标准误，这种相对排名分数不是分类准确率。[附录 A、Table 1–2](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.26457v1)
最终版本在四项汇总结果的均值上达到或超过人工版本，不代表四项都显著领先。进步也不是逐代单调：中途版本 AIDE47 在 MLE-Bench 与天气任务上优于 AIDE85。天气验证只有一个优化任务、三次不同随机设置的重复运行；它展示了一次跨任务类型迁移，不能代表已在各种科学问题上验证。
比较时也要注意预算定义。论文的外部实验有的主要限制费用，有的主要限制搜索步数；不能把全部结果概括成“完全相同 GPU 时间”。天气分数是相对起始预测程序的改善，不是 WeatherBench 排行榜的绝对成绩。**这些区别决定了收益能外推到多远。**[附录 A、Table 1–2](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.26457v1)

sections.heading: 检查代码以后，哪些漂亮机制并没有证实有效
paragraphs: 论文还检查单独测速很快的 GPU 算子，放进真实训练循环后是否仍然有效。实验有 38 个算子与训练环境的组合、每个三个种子，涉及 GPT-2、ViT 和 CNN；agent 使用 Gemini 3 Flash，每次最多搜索 20 步，算子在 NVIDIA A100 上运行。对每组先在三个种子上求平均，再按作者定义判定：单独测速超过 1.02 倍、但训练中保留不足一半所报加速或直接崩溃，就计为 reward hacking。该比例由 AIDE0 的 55% 降到 AIDE85 的 32%，人工版本为 39%。分母是 38 组场景，不是 114 次运行；相同步数也不保证相同费用或时间。这里测的是代理指标与实际效果脱节，不是在判断程序有没有主观作弊意图。[§3.4、附录 A](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.26457v1)
生成的代码里有一项惩罚异常高分候选的规则，看起来像在防止偶然赢家。但作者检查后发现它保持原有排序，重放评测时从未改变最终选中谁。因此不能把总体改善归功于这条规则，也不能仅凭程序里出现某种机制，就说它发挥了预期作用。
另一个修改修复了评估脚本的错误：原来单个测试失败会拖垮整次私有评估。修评分程序与改搜索策略是两回事。论文没有把每项改动都独立消融到足以确定贡献；目前最可靠的是完整版本的比较，机制描述应与因果证明分开。[原文 §3.5](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.26457v1)

sections.heading: 真正接近递归的下一问：它能成为更好的改写者吗
paragraphs: 假设新 agent 更擅长改分类脚本，仍不能自动推出它更擅长修改 agent 本身。两种工作虽都写代码，成功所需的判断并不相同。要让改进不断加速，就需要新版本接手后，能在可比预算内产生比旧改写者更好的后继版本。
论文为此做 ignition test：让 AIDE47 与 AIDE_human 分别担任外层改写者，从同一个内层 AIDE47 起步；每组用三个随机种子重复运行，各跑 50 步。两组平均终点相近，作者明确认为证据不足，不能断言改进版本更善于、或更高效地推动下一轮自改进。[原文 §3.6、Figure 7](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.26457v1)
所以本文展示的强证据是持续的程序优化与外部迁移；“改进能力本身持续变强”仍是待证问题。更不能从一次有限长度实验，推到不依赖更多人工设计的开放演化、无限能力增长或智能爆炸。把这个额外检验单独列出来，是它值得精读的地方。

sections.heading: 怎样阅读，并把问题带回自己的 agent 系统
paragraphs: **我们从实验提炼出的检查顺序是：** 先指出改进保存在哪里，再确认下一次运行会不会继续使用；然后问反馈是谁给的、哪个程序能看到它；最后检查测试任务有没有参与过版本选择。这样能区分一次答题修订、可复用程序改进，以及改进者本身变强。
实现上另一个未解决的问题是维护成本。复杂代码可能确实拿到更好成绩，却很难判断哪些分支有效、哪些只是遗留逻辑。研究版本的汇总成绩并不替你完成接口兼容、错误恢复和可解释性检查；论文也把这些列为部署阻力。[原文 §5](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.26457v1)
阅读路线可以按问题走：Figure 1 看内外循环；§2 看反馈与预算；Figure 5–6 看搜索和记忆；Figure 2 看连续改进；Figure 3 与附录 A 看独立任务；最后用 Figure 7 检查更强的递归主张。早期博客与论文有若干数字和实验范围差异，引用结果请统一到本篇使用的 v1。

en.contribution: Makes a research agent's control code an experimental object: propose a rewrite, have the new version complete research tasks, and retain better versions. The paper reports repeated improvements and transfer to independent tasks, then separately tests whether an improved agent is better at driving further self-improvement.
en.relevance: The question is moving beyond whether an agent can complete a research task toward whether it can improve how research is conducted. This work connects editable search decisions, context management, and experimental feedback into a measurable loop, while exposing the evidence still missing for self-acceleration.
en.reading: Today's main read; allow 35–50 minutes. First distinguish the inner loop editing task code from the outer loop editing agent code, then study search and memory. Finish with independent evaluations and the ignition test rather than stopping at the rising curve.
en.prerequisites: Only assumes that a training script can run and return a validation score. The note explains agent control code, candidate search, held-out data, and multi-armed bandits without RL or meta-learning equations.
en.caveat: The foundation models' weights and the main experiment's outer-loop proposer remain fixed. Seven accepted rewrites are not seven generations of increasingly capable self-improvers. External gains are not monotonic, the weather evaluation has one task, and promoting an evolved agent to the proposer role has no established significant advantage.

sections.heading: First improve a training script, then improve the way experiments are run
paragraphs: Suppose we give an agent an image-classification training script and ask it to improve accuracy within a limited budget. It can change the learning rate, train, inspect validation results, and decide whether to retain the change or try something else. What changes initially is the code solving a particular task. **This classification task is a teaching example used throughout this note, not a specific experiment disclosed in the paper.**

Now move up a level. Why does the agent keep making small changes to one approach? Why does it put every old log into every prompt? Could editing the program that chooses experiments, stores history, and checks results make it more effective on different future tasks? The paper calls this organizing code around the model the harness; this note also calls it agent control code.

AIDE² comes from Weco AI. The team published its initial blog on July 14, 2026 and paper v1 on September 22. This note follows the paper, a 2026 preprint. It studies persistent changes to the research tool itself, rather than treating a single rewritten answer as evidence of self-improvement. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.26457); [early team account](https://www.weco.ai/blog/first-evidence-of-recursive-self-improvement)

sections.heading: What the two loops edit, and what stays fixed
paragraphs: The inner loop receives a concrete task and repeatedly edits task code. In the classification example, it produces training scripts, executes them, records scores and errors, and submits one when its budget expires. The outer loop receives the research agent's code and edits how it selects experiments, organizes inputs, and handles feedback. Evaluating one outer-loop change requires the modified agent to carry out a suite of inner-loop tasks.

The main experiment uses the human-engineered AIDE_human as its outer-loop proposer throughout. An accepted rewrite replaces the inner-loop agent that the next round will edit. The foundation model used in each loop also stays fixed: Claude Opus 4.7 outside and Gemini 3 Flash for inner-loop evaluations. Their language-model weights are not trained here. [Paper §2.1–2.2 and Figure 1](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.26457v1)

Continuously improving one research program therefore differs from replacing the proposer with a stronger one in every generation. The main experiment does the former; the latter requires another test. Fixed language-model weights do not prohibit the inner task from training a classifier. The restriction concerns the model driving the agent, not the research work it executes.

sections.heading: Three levels of feedback guard against different mistakes
paragraphs: Return to classification. The agent repeatedly sees a public validation score and uses it to choose its next experiment. Enough attempts may nevertheless find a script tailored to that validation data. The submitted solution is therefore scored on private data the inner agent cannot see. The outer loop aggregates private scores across tasks to decide whether to retain the agent rewrite. [Paper §2.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.26457v1)

Private here means hidden from the inner solver. Because the outer loop repeatedly uses the aggregate to choose versions, that score still participates in development and cannot establish final generalization. A third level is needed: freeze selected agents and evaluate them on new tasks that never affected version selection. This distinguishes doing better on the selection tasks from a transferable research method.

**Our interpretation of the three levels is:** public feedback asks how to change the next task solution; the private grade asks whether to keep this agent version; independent external evaluation asks whether the retained changes help on new tasks. All three may be called evaluation, but their roles differ. Data hidden from one level is not necessarily unused test data for the whole system.

sections.heading: Search: avoid betting the entire budget on the current leader
paragraphs: The initial agent tends to keep improving its highest-scoring candidate. In the teaching example, if learning-rate tuning narrowly beats a preprocessing change, most subsequent attempts might go to the former. But preprocessing might only need further refinement; always chasing the current leader can abandon another promising direction too early. Starting a wholly new approach every time would instead discard accumulated progress.

The final agent, AIDE85, groups drafting strategies into five categories, selects a strategy, then expands the best candidate carrying that strategy. Strategy selection uses a multi-armed bandit: allocate another attempt using both previous returns and how insufficiently explored an option remains. The paper specifically uses UCB1 mixed with another score-based sampling choice, and periodically continues the best solution under a different strategy. [Paper §3.5 and Figure 5](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.26457v1)

This need not invent an entirely new research direction. It changes how experimental effort is distributed: useful existing code can survive while the angle of the next attempt changes. **Our classification analogy is:** retain the best training script, but let a different optimization approach continue from it.

sections.heading: Memory: retain records that can change the next decision
paragraphs: After 30 experiments, sending all 30 scripts and every log makes the input progressively longer. A call intended only to fix an import error still processes many irrelevant successful runs. Deleting all history is also inadequate because the agent may repeat failed attempts. The issue is choosing information, not assuming that a longer input necessarily provides better memory.

AIDE85 switches to shorter, role-specific inputs. Drafting and improvement read summaries of the root solution and recent candidates; recurring error records are added when bugs become frequent. Unlike the starting version, it no longer continually concatenates the complete history. This change lives in the control program and persists across subsequent tasks. [Paper §3.5 and Figure 6](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.26457v1)

**A practical implication of this mechanism is:** when calls and execution are cost-constrained, removing irrelevant input can leave budget for more useful attempts. But shorter inputs do not guarantee better results; dropping an important counterexample can worsen decisions. The whole research task must still be evaluated. A compression ratio is not automatically the same multiplier in research speed.

sections.heading: How many improvements actually lie inside the eight-day curve
paragraphs: The main run lasts eight days and contains 100 nodes: the initial agent plus 99 rewrite proposals. Seven replace the incumbent, taking the aggregate private grade from 0.703 to 0.778. Two further complete runs accept two and four rewrites. This is evidence of repeatedly finding useful changes, not of every attempt succeeding. [Paper §3.2 and Figure 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.26457v1)

The values 0.703 and 0.778 are aggregate selection grades, not a statement that general research ability rises from 70.3% to 77.8%. An incumbent curve retains the best version so far and therefore does not fall when worse candidates are rejected. The relevant questions are how many candidates were attempted, whether acceptance was reliable, and how those versions perform independently.

Humans still define the starting system, task collection, per-task budgets, and acceptance rule; the loop automates proposals, execution, and comparison during the run. The team reports no human intervention inside that loop, which is different from no human design. Comparing eight days with the team's preceding two years of development provides context, but does not establish a matched-condition multiplier for replacing researchers. [Team account](https://www.weco.ai/blog/first-evidence-of-recursive-self-improvement)

sections.heading: Do the improvements survive a different set of research tasks?
paragraphs: The authors compare the initial, intermediate, final, and human-engineered agents on ALE-Bench, MLE-Bench, FML-Bench, and a weather task based on WeatherBench 2, none used for selection. The first three cover algorithm or ML engineering, while weather tests optimization of a physics-based forecasting program absent from the selection families. Within each benchmark, all agents follow the same protocol. [Paper §3.3 and Appendix A](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.26457v1)

For a concrete ML-engineering comparison, MLE-Bench lite contains 22 competitions with three seeds per task. All agents use Gemini 3 Flash with a primary budget of $5 per run; solution scripts execute in CPU containers with 4–24 vCPUs and 16–192 GB RAM. Mean private percentile rises from 0.678±0.006 for AIDE0 to 0.722±0.011 for AIDE85, versus 0.708±0.007 for the human-engineered agent. The ± denotes one standard error. This relative-ranking metric is not classification accuracy. [Appendix A, Tables 1–2](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.26457v1).

The final version matches or exceeds the human-engineered agent in all four aggregate means; this does not establish significant superiority on all four. Improvement is not monotonic: intermediate AIDE47 beats AIDE85 on MLE-Bench and weather. The weather evaluation contains only one optimization task and three seeds. It demonstrates one transfer across task types, not validation across scientific research generally.

Budget definitions also matter. Some external experiments primarily constrain cost and others search steps, so the entire collection cannot be described as using identical GPU time. The weather number measures improvement relative to its starting forecasting program, not an absolute WeatherBench leaderboard score. **These distinctions determine how far the measured benefit can be extrapolated.** [Appendix A and Tables 1–2](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.26457v1)

sections.heading: Which appealing code mechanisms lack evidence of effectiveness?
paragraphs: The paper also checks whether fast isolated GPU kernels remain effective inside actual training loops. The experiment covers 38 kernel/context pairs with three seeds each, spanning GPT-2, ViT, and CNN training. Agents use Gemini 3 Flash with at most 20 search steps, and kernels run on NVIDIA A100 GPUs. After averaging speedups across seeds for each pair, the authors count reward hacking when isolated speedup exceeds 1.02× but less than half the reported speedup survives in training, or the kernel crashes there. The rate falls from 55% for AIDE0 to 32% for AIDE85, versus 39% for the human-engineered agent. The denominator is 38 pairs, not 114 runs, and equal step budgets do not imply equal cost or runtime. This measures a disconnect between a proxy and actual outcomes, not an intention to cheat. [§3.4, Appendix A](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.26457v1).

The generated code includes a rule penalizing unusually high-scoring candidates, apparently intended to avoid lucky winners. Inspection shows that it preserves the existing ranking and never changes the selected candidate when evaluations are replayed. The overall improvement therefore cannot be credited to that rule. A mechanism appearing in code does not establish that it performs its intended role.

Another change repairs an evaluation-script defect: one failing test previously brought down the entire private evaluation. Repairing scoring code differs from improving search policy. The paper does not independently ablate every change sufficiently to assign its contribution; whole-version comparisons are stronger evidence than individual mechanistic attributions. [Paper §3.5](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.26457v1)

sections.heading: The next recursive question: does it become a better proposer?
paragraphs: Even if a new agent is better at modifying classification scripts, it need not be better at modifying agents. Both involve writing code, but require different judgments. For improvement to accelerate, a new version taking over the proposer role must produce better successors than the old proposer could under comparable resources.

The paper tests this with an ignition experiment: AIDE47 and AIDE_human separately drive the outer loop, both starting from the same inner AIDE47. Each arm has three seeds and runs for 50 steps. Their average endpoints are similar. The authors explicitly regard the evidence as inconclusive: it does not establish that the evolved version drives further self-improvement better or more efficiently. [Paper §3.6 and Figure 7](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.26457v1)

The strong evidence here is therefore repeated program optimization and external transfer; continuously improving the ability to improve remains unproven. One finite experiment also cannot establish open-ended evolution without additional human design, unlimited capability growth, or an intelligence explosion. Isolating this stronger test is one reason the paper deserves a close read.

sections.heading: A reading route and questions to bring back to an agent system
paragraphs: **The inspection sequence we infer from these experiments is:** identify where an improvement is stored and whether the next run will reuse it; determine who supplies feedback and which program can see it; then check whether evaluation tasks participated in choosing versions. This distinguishes revision of one answer, reusable program improvement, and improvement of the proposer itself.

Maintenance remains another unresolved issue. Complex generated code may score better while leaving it difficult to tell which branches matter and which are residue. A research aggregate does not perform compatibility, error-recovery, and interpretability checks for deployment. The paper also identifies these as practical obstacles. [Paper §5](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.26457v1)

Read by question: Figure 1 for the two loops; §2 for feedback and budgets; Figures 5–6 for search and memory; Figure 2 for repeated gains; Figure 3 and Appendix A for independent tasks; and finally Figure 7 for the stronger recursive claim. The early blog and paper differ in several numbers and evaluation scope, so use the v1 paper consistently when citing results.

zh.contribution: 同一个模型看过示范后，往往比没看时更会做题。SDFT 让没看示范的学生先自己作答，再向看过示范的教师学习，更新模型权重。在论文的有限任务序列中，它比直接模仿示范更能兼顾新技能和原有能力。
zh.relevance: 与修改 agent 程序相区别，这篇改变的是模型本身。它帮助判断：什么时候应把经验留在输入里，什么时候值得付出生成、教师计算和训练成本，让模型以后不看示范也能使用。
zh.reading: 选读，值得精读 §3 / Fig. 2、§4.3 / Fig. 3、Table 5，再看附录 A.3 的教师稳定性。建议 30–40 分钟；先理解教师和学生各看到了什么，再读 KL 公式。
zh.prerequisites: 从一个工具调用例子开始，解释模型权重、监督微调、蒸馏和当前模型自己生成训练过程的含义。不要求先学过强化学习算法。
zh.caveat: 方法需要外部示范，连续学习证据主要是三个技能依次训练，并非无限期自主学习。原有能力仍可能下降；小模型也可能不如普通微调。理论的 reverse KL 与 v2 所述实际采用的 forward KL 必须区分。

sections.heading: 看一眼正确示范就会做，能不能下次不看也会
paragraphs: **教学例子，不是论文实验题：**给模型一个天气工具的说明，让它查询上海气温。模型可能选对工具，却填错参数；如果再给它这道题的正确调用示范，它就更容易理解应该怎样回答。问题是，把示范拿走以后，这个改进还能不能留下？
SDFT 把模型分成两个角色：学生只看问题，教师额外看到示范。训练让学生向教师学习，改变决定它怎样生成文字的数值，也就是模型权重。这样，下一次作答依靠的是训练后的模型，不必每次把原示范重新塞进输入。“自己教自己”的教师仍然得到了外部信息。

论文由 Idan Shenfeld、Mehul Damani、Jonas Hübotter、Pulkit Agrawal 完成，来自 MIT 与 ETH Zürich，已发表于 ICML 2026。初稿为 2026 年 1 月；下文机制和实验细节按 8 月 7 日 arXiv v2 核对。[正式会议记录](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v306/shenfeld26a.html)；[v2 原文](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.19897v2)

sections.heading: 学生先写自己的答案，教师再沿着这条路指导
paragraphs: 普通监督微调，简称 SFT，会让模型模仿数据集里的示范答案。SDFT 则先让当前学生只根据问题生成一次回答。这样得到的是学生按自己的习惯走出的过程，可能与专家示范不同；用当前模型自己生成的过程来训练，称为 on-policy。
随后，教师读取问题、示范，以及学生已经写出的前缀，计算接下来各种 token 的概率。token 是模型处理文字的基本单位。学生也在相同前缀处给出概率，训练会让这两组预测更接近。这种向另一个模型的预测学习的方式叫蒸馏；这里不是只拿一个最终对错分数，也不是把学生回答全部替换成示范。
回到天气例子，教师知道正确调用应是什么，学生却必须练习自己从问题出发组织答案。测试时，只给训练后的学生问题和正常任务输入，不提供教师额外看到的示范。原文 Fig. 6 还与“提前生成教师答案，再训练学生”的做法比较，检验收益是否只来自更好的教师。[§3、§4.6、Fig. 2 / 6](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19897v2)

sections.heading: 教师怎样跟着变强，又不跟着每一步波动
paragraphs: 教师和学生从同一模型出发，但训练中不能简单当成两份始终相同的模型。v2 默认让教师保留大部分旧权重，只逐步混入学生的新权重。这叫指数移动平均，简称 EMA。教师因此能跟上学生的进步，又不会立刻追随每一次更新的波动。
附录 A.3 比较了三种教师：始终冻结的基础模型较稳定，但效果较弱；直接使用当前学生作教师容易不稳定；EMA 在该实验中兼顾了两者。它不是免费增加一个更强的外部模型，也不保证教师每次判断都对。

衡量两组生成概率差异的方法叫 KL 散度，而且比较方向不同，训练目标也不同。**§3 的理论推导使用 reverse KL；实际实现说明则报告 forward KL 表现最好。** 不能把前者的理论解释直接当成后者完整的保证。第一次读可以先记住：学生自己产生练习过程，教师提供每一步的概率指导；方向和估计方法留到复现时核对。[§3、附录 A.1 / A.3](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19897v2)

sections.heading: 训练信息从哪里来，哪些工作仍由外部安排
paragraphs: 主实验使用 Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct，并训练全部模型参数；附录给出的训练硬件是单张 NVIDIA H200。技能包括科学问答、工具调用、医学问答。科学示范由 GPT-4o 对训练题最多尝试八次，保留最终答案正确的一份；工具调用示范来自 ToolAlpaca；医学训练使用约两万道英文题，另取一千道可验证问题评估。
数据准备和选模型并非自主完成。研究者划分训练、验证和测试集，搜索学习率等设置，再按验证集成绩选择模型；医学评估使用 GPT-5-mini。训练本身不要求另写一个奖励函数，但正确示范、已有答案和评估方法依然提供了外部帮助。“没有显式奖励”不能改写成“没有监督”。
另一个知识实验整理约二十万 token 的文章，描述模型知识截止时间之后的 2025 年自然灾害。GPT-5 据此生成问答，人还检查重复问题。知识实验的教师同时看到文章与示范回答，学生没有这些额外材料；实验并非模型自行发现新闻、判断真假再决定学什么。[§4.1、附录 A.2 / B](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19897v2)

sections.heading: 学会新任务之后，原来会的是否还会
paragraphs: 先看 ToolAlpaca 的单任务比较。Table 5 中，Qwen2.5-7B 基础模型正确率为 42.9%，普通 SFT 为 63.2%，SDFT 为 70.6%。再测六项原有能力，其平均分分别是 65.5、56.0、65.4。这里支持的是：新任务更好，同时原有能力平均下降较少；不能据一个平均数说每项能力都完全保住。
更接近连续学习的是 Fig. 3：同一个模型依次学习前面三个技能，每换一个任务仍检查先前技能。SDFT 比顺序 SFT 更能保留已经学到的内容。不过这只是一条有限的三任务序列，并非几个月不停接收真实用户经验。图的纵轴还按各任务基础分和最高分做了归一化，不能直接读成百分比正确率。
准确率评估用每一步选最高概率 token 的 greedy 生成；附录说明通常运行三个随机种子。作者也检查多次尝试至少成功一次的 pass@k，最高到 128，收益仍存在。这增加了证据，但仍不能代替跨更多任务、顺序和时间的验证。[§4.2–4.3、Fig. 3 / 5、附录 B.2、Table 5](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19897v2)

sections.heading: 把新事实留进权重，效果和代价各是什么
paragraphs: 在灾害知识实验中，答案细节必须全部正确时，SFT 得 80%，SDFT 得 89%；换成不直接点名原事件、但需要相关知识的问题，分别为 80% 和 98%。这些结果来自所构造的小范围知识任务和自动评估，不能推广为所有新知识都能稳定学会。每次都提供正确文章的理想检索对照，仍分别达到 91% 和 100%。
模型首先要能读懂示范。科学问答的规模比较中，3B 模型用 SDFT 反而落后普通 SFT。作者还报告，学生会学到教师的“根据上述文本”等措辞，尽管学生实际上没收到那段文本。把有用知识学进去时，也可能一起学到不适用的表达习惯。[§4.2、§4.4、§5](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19897v2)
相比普通 SFT，这套训练还增加学生生成和教师计算概率的成本，然后才更新学生权重。每题只生成一次，并不意味着一次普通推理的费用。实际成本取决于生成长度、训练轮数和实现，应把这些环节分别测量；论文给出的整体倍率没有充分交代每项比较条件，因此这里不把它当作通用预算依据。[§5、附录 B.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19897v2)

sections.heading: 它证明了哪种改进，怎样读才不会混在一起
paragraphs: 这里保存下来的改进在模型权重里；学习算法、任务和示范来源仍由外部规定。论文没有展示模型自主重写自己的学习方法，再持续提高改进自身的能力，所以不能仅凭“自蒸馏”就称为递归自我改进。作者也承认仍有遗忘，处理低质量示范或用户对话属于后续方向。
**对系统工作的以下联系是我们的分析：**如果采用这种训练，需要分别测学生生成、教师评分和参数更新的成本，并保证教师与学生在同一段已生成内容上比较概率。上线后不再携带原示范，是以提前训练为代价；是否划算，要与检索或把示范放进上下文的方式共同比较。
先读 Fig. 2，画清教师比学生多看了什么；再读 Fig. 3 和 Table 5，区分新任务分数与原有能力；最后读附录 A.3 和 §5，检查稳定性、费用及失败情形。理解这些之后再看 §3 的 KL 推导，才不容易把“借助示范学得更好”误读成“模型已能无条件持续自我进化”。

en.contribution: A model often performs better after seeing a demonstration. SDFT lets a student without that demonstration generate its own response, then learn from a demonstration-conditioned teacher through weight updates. In the paper's finite task sequence, this better balances new skills and existing capabilities than directly imitating demonstrations.
en.relevance: This changes the model itself, unlike modifying an agent program. It helps assess when experience should remain in the input and when generation, teacher computation, and training costs are worth paying so that future responses no longer require the demonstration.
en.reading: Optional and worth reading: §3 / Fig. 2, §4.3 / Fig. 3, and Table 5, followed by the teacher-stability study in Appendix A.3. Allow 30–40 minutes. Understand what each role can see before working through the KL equations.
en.prerequisites: A tool-calling example introduces model weights, supervised fine-tuning, distillation, and training on responses generated by the current model. No prior reinforcement-learning derivation is required.
en.caveat: The method needs external demonstrations, and the main sequential evidence covers three skills rather than indefinite autonomous learning. Some prior capabilities can still decline, and small models can underperform ordinary fine-tuning. Distinguish the theoretical reverse-KL objective from the forward KL reported for the v2 implementation.

sections.heading: Can improvement from seeing a demonstration survive after it is removed?
paragraphs: **Explanatory example, not a paper benchmark item:** give a model a weather-tool specification and ask for Shanghai's temperature. It might choose the right tool but supply the wrong arguments. Showing the correct call for this training question can help it understand the required response. Can that improvement survive when the demonstration is removed?

SDFT assigns two roles to the model: the student sees the question, while the teacher additionally sees a demonstration. Training makes the student learn from the teacher by changing the numerical parameters governing generation—its model weights. Future responses can then use the trained model without repeatedly inserting the original demonstration. The self-teacher still receives external information.

The paper is by Idan Shenfeld, Mehul Damani, Jonas Hübotter, and Pulkit Agrawal, from MIT and ETH Zürich, and appeared at ICML 2026. The first preprint was posted in January 2026. The mechanism and experimental details below follow arXiv v2, dated August 7. [Official proceedings](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v306/shenfeld26a.html); [v2 paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.19897v2).

sections.heading: The student writes first; the teacher guides along that trajectory
paragraphs: Ordinary supervised fine-tuning, or SFT, trains a model to imitate demonstration answers from a dataset. SDFT instead first lets the current student generate one response from the question alone. This follows the student's own habits and may differ from the expert demonstration. Training on behavior generated by the current model is called on-policy learning.

The teacher then reads the question, demonstration, and the prefix already generated by the student, and computes probabilities for the next token. Tokens are the basic units of text processed by the model. The student also predicts probabilities at the same prefix, and training brings the predictions closer. Learning from another model's predictions is called distillation. The signal is richer than one final correctness score, and the student's response is not simply replaced by the demonstration.

In the weather example, the teacher knows what a correct call should look like, while the student practices producing an answer from the question. At test time, the trained student receives the question and ordinary task inputs without the teacher's privileged demonstration. Figure 6 also compares this approach with generating teacher answers in advance and then training the student, testing whether teacher quality alone explains the improvement. [§3, §4.6, Figs. 2 and 6](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19897v2).

sections.heading: How does the teacher improve without following every fluctuation?
paragraphs: Teacher and student start from the same model, but they should not be treated as identical throughout training. By default, v2 retains most of the teacher's previous weights and gradually mixes in the student's new weights. This exponential moving average, or EMA, lets the teacher track progress without immediately following every update.

Appendix A.3 compares three teachers. A frozen base model is stable but weaker; using the current student directly can be unstable; EMA provides a better balance in the experiment. This does not introduce a stronger external teacher for free, nor does it guarantee that every teacher judgment is correct.

KL divergence measures differences between probability distributions, and its direction matters. **The theoretical derivation in §3 uses reverse KL, whereas the practical implementation discussion reports the best results with forward KL.** The former's theoretical interpretation cannot simply be treated as a complete guarantee for the latter. On a first reading, retain the execution order: student-generated practice followed by token-level probability guidance. The objective direction and estimator deserve separate attention when reproducing the method. [§3, Appendices A.1 and A.3](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19897v2).

sections.heading: Where does the training information come from?
paragraphs: The main experiments use Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and fine-tune all model parameters; the appendix specifies a single NVIDIA H200 for training. Skills include scientific questions, tool calling, and medical questions. Science demonstrations are produced by asking GPT-4o up to eight times per training question and retaining a response with the correct final answer. Tool demonstrations come from ToolAlpaca. The medical experiment uses approximately 20,000 English training questions and 1,000 separately sampled verifiable evaluation questions.

Data preparation and model selection are externally organized. Researchers define training, validation, and test sets, search settings such as learning rates, and select checkpoints by validation performance. Medical evaluation uses GPT-5-mini. Training does not require a separately engineered reward function, but demonstrations, known answers, and evaluation procedures still provide external assistance. No explicit reward does not mean no supervision.

A separate knowledge experiment assembles approximately 200,000 tokens of articles about 2025 natural disasters after the model's knowledge cutoff. GPT-5 generates question–answer pairs, and humans check for duplicate questions. The teacher sees both the article and a worked answer, while the student lacks those additional materials. The experiment does not involve the model independently discovering news, establishing its truth, and deciding what to learn. [§4.1, Appendices A.2 and B](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19897v2).

sections.heading: After learning a new task, does the model retain its old abilities?
paragraphs: Consider the single-task ToolAlpaca comparison in Table 5. Qwen2.5-7B scores 42.9% before adaptation, 63.2% after ordinary SFT, and 70.6% after SDFT. Average scores across six prior-capability benchmarks are 65.5, 56.0, and 65.4, respectively. This supports stronger new-task performance with less average degradation. It does not establish that every prior ability is perfectly preserved.

Figure 3 more directly tests sequential learning: one model learns the three skills in succession, while earlier skills continue to be evaluated. SDFT retains earlier learning better than sequential SFT. This remains a finite three-task sequence, not months of continuous adaptation to real users. Its vertical axis is also normalized separately using each task's base and maximum scores; it is not a percentage-accuracy axis.

Accuracy uses greedy generation, choosing the highest-probability token at each step. The appendix reports three random seeds unless otherwise specified. The authors also measure pass@k—the chance that at least one of k attempts succeeds—up to k = 128, where gains persist. This adds evidence but does not replace evaluation over more tasks, task orders, and time horizons. [§4.2–4.3, Figs. 3 and 5, Appendix B.2, Table 5](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19897v2).

sections.heading: What are the gains and costs of storing new facts in weights?
paragraphs: On the disaster-knowledge experiment, strict accuracy requiring all answer details to be correct is 80% for SFT and 89% for SDFT. For indirect questions that require the new knowledge without explicitly naming the original event, the scores are 80% and 98%. These results concern a narrowly constructed knowledge task with automated evaluation, not all possible factual updates. An ideal retrieval baseline that always supplies the correct article still scores 91% and 100%, respectively.

The model must first be capable of using a demonstration. In the science-task scaling study, the 3B model underperforms ordinary SFT when trained with SDFT. The authors also observe that students can inherit phrases such as references to an accompanying text even when no such text was supplied to them. Useful knowledge and inappropriate wording can be learned together. [§4.2, §4.4, §5](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19897v2).

Compared with ordinary SFT, this training adds student generation and teacher probability computation before updating student weights. One generated response per question does not make it as cheap as one inference call. Costs depend on generated length, training epochs, and implementation, so these stages should be measured separately. The paper does not fully specify the matched conditions behind its overall cost ratios; this note therefore does not use them as a general budgeting rule. [§5, Appendix B.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19897v2).

sections.heading: What kind of improvement does this establish?
paragraphs: The persistent change is in model weights, while the learning algorithm, tasks, and demonstration sources remain externally specified. The paper does not show a model autonomously rewriting its learning method and repeatedly improving its ability to improve itself. Self-distillation therefore does not by itself establish recursive self-improvement. The authors acknowledge remaining forgetting and leave noisy demonstrations and user conversations as future directions.

**The following systems connection is our analysis:** an implementation should separately measure student generation, teacher scoring, and parameter updates, while ensuring that teacher and student compare probabilities on the same generated prefix. Removing demonstrations from deployment inputs is purchased through earlier training. Whether that trade is worthwhile requires comparison with retrieval or supplying demonstrations in context.

Read Fig. 2 first and identify the information available only to the teacher. Then use Fig. 3 and Table 5 to separate new-task gains from retention. Finish with Appendix A.3 and §5 for stability, cost, and failure cases. Only then return to the KL derivation in §3, keeping improvement from supplied demonstrations distinct from unconditional, ongoing self-evolution.

papers.title: Which Self-Improvements Should We Trust? Reliable Self-Improvement When Agents Reuse Their Benchmarks

zh.contribution: 研究反复用同一批题筛选改动时，怎样避免把碰巧涨分当作真实进步；限制评测反馈，并为整个搜索过程分配允许的误判风险。
zh.relevance: 为 AIDE² 这类不断修改程序、按评测决定保留版本的系统补上一道问题：留下来的改动，究竟改善了同一目标分布中新样本的表现，还是越来越适合这套考试？
zh.reading: 值得选读，建议 20–30 分钟。先理解考试例子，再读 §2.1 的假设、Algorithm 1、Table 1，最后核对附录 B 的预筛与消融。
zh.prerequisites: 只需知道分类器根据输入作判断，开发集用于调试，另留数据检查泛化。正文解释重复比较、配对检验与风险预算，无需先读完统计证明。
zh.caveat: 2026 年预印本，实测只有 Covertype 上受限的分类器配置搜索。独立保留集也只是总体表现的估计；零次误接纳不是零风险，理论要求初始独立、同分布抽样与严格限制反馈。

sections.heading: 题目没有泄露，为什么还是可能越考越偏
paragraphs: **下面是教学例子，不是论文数据。** 让 Agent 修改一个分类器，每次交八个版本，评测服务只返回准确率。第一次，它发现加深决策树得分最高；下一次便围绕深度继续改。题目始终藏在服务器里，但分数已经在指导搜索。多轮以后，程序可能越来越适合这批题，却没有同样改善新样本的判断。
这里不必发生直接偷看答案。选出高分版本，再根据成绩决定下一步，本身就在利用评测信息；这种越试越迎合固定评测集的现象叫适应性过拟合。REUSE 专门研究这个问题。论文来自 Purdue University，2026 年 9 月 27 日首发，本篇读 9 月 29 日 v2；目前按预印本介绍。[版本与作者](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.33180v2)

sections.heading: 一轮挑八个，与连续改很多轮，是两层问题
paragraphs: 只看一轮，八个版本里最好的那个，也可能只是碰巧更适合这批样本。不断重复比较，又增加了至少误判一次的机会。若所有候选事先确定，可以为这些比较分配更小的误判额度；但 Agent 会看前面的反馈，再提出后面的版本，候选就不再独立于这批评测题。只按总比较次数收紧门槛，没有自动解决这一层依赖。
REUSE 让提出改动的一侧充分使用另一份开发数据，但评测服务只回传“全部拒绝”或“接受第几个候选”。原始分数、逐题结果，以及内部算出的改进保证都不回传。接受决定仍然包含信息，所以方法还要把可能出现的决定历史纳入风险计算，不能认为隐藏分数就万事大吉。[§1–2](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.33180v2)

sections.heading: 怎么决定接受，以及保证到底保证什么
paragraphs: 在对错评分中，服务把新旧版本放到相同题目上比较：新版本修好了多少原来的错误，又弄错了多少原来答对的题？两者都对或都错的题，不提供胜负证据。配对检验据此判断，新版本的优势能否仅由抽样波动解释；再按本轮候选数、此前接受次数和可能历史收紧接受门槛。

理论前提很严格：评测样本来自同一个目标分布，彼此独立，也就是 i.i.d.；它最初必须独立于开发数据、初始系统和搜索随机性；后续只通过规定的决定传递信息。设整个过程允许的错误概率 α 为 0.05，结论是在这些条件下，以至少 95% 的概率，所有被接受的改动都提高该分布上的平均表现。这是对评测集抽样下整段过程的共同保证，不是对已经观察到的某次更新给出 95% 的后验可信度，也不是每次更新单独有 95% 把握，更不是绝不会退步。
已有题目污染、额外日志回传或部署任务改变，都不能直接套用这个保证。越往后通常还要更强的证据，真正的小进步可能被拒绝。因此，方法控制的是错误接纳，不承诺永远找到下一次进步。[§2.1、Theorem 1、Proposition 1](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.33180v2)

sections.heading: 真实实验改的是分类器配置，不是完整研究 Agent
paragraphs: 实验用 Covertype 数据判断一个样本是否属于第 2 类森林覆盖类型。Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct 通过 vLLM 在一张 A100 40GB 上提出 scikit-learn 配置，模型家族限定为梯度提升与逻辑回归；每个候选最多改两个字段，如学习率、特征子集或预处理。每次搜索有 200 轮，每轮最多八个有效候选，两种评测集大小各跑 30 个种子。[§3.1、附录 B.1–B.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.33180v2)

作者把数据分成五万条训练样本、两万条开发样本、六万条评测池与五万条最终保留样本。每次从评测池抽两千或一万条，反复用于接受决策；最终保留集 H 不给任何搜索方法访问，用来另行检查改动。人工预先规定任务、配置空间、提示词和检查规则；论文没有描述逐轮人工选优。这仍是受限的自动搜索，不能写成 Agent 自主完成了 200 次能力跃迁。 搜索中不训练提出建议的语言模型；变化的是分类器配置，每个分类器再用训练集拟合。

sections.heading: 少接受一些改动，最后的成绩仍然接近
paragraphs: Table 1 的两千条评测样本条件下，REUSE 平均每次搜索接受 3.2 个改动，30 次搜索合计未观察到错误接纳；最终在 H 上比起始分类器提高 7.02±0.26 个百分点。直接挑评测涨分最多的版本，平均接受 13.0 个改动，出现 75 次错误接纳，最终提高 7.04±0.08 个百分点。这里的 ± 是标准误，错误接纳指改动在 H 上没有正收益。[Table 1](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.33180v2)
因此，最终分数接近，不代表中间每次更新都可靠。另一条更保守的 Bonferroni-style 基线也没有错误接纳，但该条件下最终只提高 2.35±0.37 个百分点。不能据此声称只有 REUSE 能做到零次错误，也不能把论文的 SICA-style、DGM-style 配置搜索当作原始系统的完整复现。五万条 H 仍是有限样本，“真实进步”在实验里也是估计；这里没有外部团队独立复现的证据。

sections.heading: 不能把全部收益都归给最后一道统计检验
paragraphs: 附录披露 REUSE 还使用开发集上的草稿更新与提交预筛，并去掉已经评测过的重复配置；其他方法收到的信息与搜索方式并不完全相同。因此主表比较的是组合流程。开发集上的尝试轮次，也不应直接等同于正式查询评测集的次数。[附录 B，Table 2–3、6](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.33180v2)

更直接的证据来自移除检验的实验：作者把开发集缩到 500 条、放宽预筛，在十个新种子上制造较容易误选的条件。保留评测检验时，九个在 H 上没有正收益的候选被拒绝，47 次接受里没有错误；去掉检验后，十次运行中有五次出现错误接纳，合计六次。两边最终成绩没有显著差异。这支持检验对更新可靠性的作用，仍不证明开放式代码或长程 Agent 都会获得同样效果。[附录 B.4.1、Figure 4](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.33180v2)

sections.heading: 与今天主读一起看，要追问哪几件事
paragraphs: **以下是阅读与工程建议。** 看自动改程序、写记忆或改训练流程的系统时，先追踪评测反馈走向：谁能看分数，谁据此提出下一版，最终审计数据有没有再进入调试？开发数据可以反复用来找方向，但不能仅因另一批题从未直接显示给 Agent，就把反复查询它们当成独立验证。 例如，AIDE² 的外层会看到选拔成绩；它没有直接满足 REUSE 的“只回传接受决定”限制，不能把这里的统计保证套到主读实验上。
精读顺序是 §2.1 的假设、Algorithm 1、Table 1，再读附录 B 的信息表和消融；统计推导可留到需要实现时。与 AIDE² 配对的价值，是把“能提出有用改动”与“怎样可信地决定保留改动”接起来。REUSE 给出有条件的评测方案，尚未实证验证通用研究 Agent 的持续自我提升。[v2 全文](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.33180v2)

en.contribution: Studies how repeated selection on a fixed evaluation set can mistake chance gains for genuine progress. It limits evaluation feedback and budgets the risk of erroneous promotion across the search.
en.relevance: Adds a question for systems such as AIDE² that revise programs and retain versions using evaluation: do the retained changes improve performance on new examples from the same target distribution, or increasingly suit this particular exam?
en.reading: Worth an optional close read; allow 20–30 minutes. Start with the exam example, then read the assumptions in Section 2.1, Algorithm 1, and Table 1, followed by Appendix B's screening details and ablations.
en.prerequisites: Only assumes that a classifier predicts from inputs, development data guides debugging, and separate data checks generalization. The note explains repeated comparisons, paired testing, and error budgets before any statistical proofs.
en.caveat: A 2026 preprint tested only on constrained classifier-configuration search using Covertype. The separate holdout still estimates population performance; zero observed false promotions does not mean zero risk. The theorem requires initial independence, i.i.d. sampling, and strictly limited feedback.

sections.heading: How an unseen exam can still steer search in the wrong direction
paragraphs: **This is a teaching example, not a result from the paper.** An agent revises a classifier, submits eight versions at a time, and receives only accuracy from an evaluation service. A deeper decision tree scores highest on the first round, so the agent explores depth next. The questions remain on the server, but their scores already guide the search. After many rounds, the program may fit these particular questions increasingly well without improving equally on new examples.

No direct access to answers is necessary. Keeping a high-scoring version and choosing the next experiment from its score already uses evaluation information. This gradual fitting to a repeatedly consulted set is adaptive overfitting, the problem REUSE studies. The authors are at Purdue University. The preprint first appeared on September 27, 2026; this note uses v2 dated September 29 and presents it as a preprint. [Version and authors](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.33180v2)

sections.heading: Choosing among eight versions differs from adapting over many rounds
paragraphs: Within one round, the best of eight versions might simply be unusually lucky on this sample. Repeated comparisons also increase the chance of making at least one mistake. If candidates were fixed beforehand, one could allocate smaller error allowances to these comparisons. But an agent uses previous feedback to propose later versions, making those candidates dependent on the evaluation set. Tightening a threshold only by the total number of comparisons does not automatically address that dependence.

REUSE lets the proposer freely use separate development data, while the evaluation service returns only that all candidates were rejected or the index of the accepted candidate. It withholds raw scores, per-example outcomes, and its internal improvement certificate. Acceptance decisions still carry information, so the method must also account for the possible decision histories. Hiding the score alone is insufficient. [Sections 1–2](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.33180v2)

sections.heading: How acceptance works, and what the guarantee actually covers
paragraphs: For pass/fail evaluation, the service compares the old and new systems on the same questions. How many former errors does the new version fix, and how many formerly correct answers does it break? Questions both versions pass or both fail provide no win–loss evidence. A paired test assesses whether sampling variation can explain the apparent advantage. The acceptance threshold also accounts for the number of candidates, earlier promotions, and possible histories.

The theoretical conditions are strict. Evaluation examples must be independent draws from one target distribution: i.i.d. The set must initially be independent of development data, the starting system, and the proposer's randomness. Subsequently it may influence search only through the prescribed decisions. With an error budget α of 0.05 for the entire process, the result is that, under these conditions, with probability at least 95%, every accepted change improves average performance on that distribution. This is a joint guarantee over evaluation-set sampling for the whole process, not a 95% posterior confidence for an already observed update. It is not a separate 95% assurance for each update, and it does not mean regression is impossible.

Prior contamination, additional feedback through logs, or a changed deployment distribution cannot simply inherit this guarantee. Later stages generally require stronger evidence, so genuine small improvements may be rejected. The method controls false acceptance; it does not promise to keep finding progress. [Section 2.1, Theorem 1, Proposition 1](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.33180v2)

sections.heading: The experiment changes classifier settings, not a complete research agent
paragraphs: The experiment uses Covertype to predict whether an example belongs to forest cover type 2. Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct proposes scikit-learn configurations through vLLM on one A100 40GB, restricted to gradient boosting and logistic regression. Each candidate changes at most two fields, such as learning rate, feature subset, or preprocessing. A search lasts 200 rounds with up to eight valid candidates per round, and each of two evaluation-set sizes is tested over 30 seeds. [Section 3.1, Appendices B.1–B.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.33180v2)

The authors separate 50,000 training examples, 20,000 development examples, a 60,000-example evaluation pool, and a 50,000-example final holdout. A run draws 2,000 or 10,000 examples from the pool and reuses them for acceptance decisions. No search method accesses the final holdout H, which separately checks changes. Humans define the task, configuration space, prompts, and validation rules in advance; the paper describes no human selection at each round. This remains constrained automated search, not 200 autonomous leaps in agent capability. The proposing language model is not trained during search; classifier configurations change, and each classifier is fitted on the training split.

sections.heading: Accepting fewer changes can still reach a similar final score
paragraphs: In Table 1's 2,000-example evaluation condition, REUSE accepts an average of 3.2 changes per search, with no observed false promotions across 30 searches. Its final improvement over the initial classifier on H is 7.02±0.26 percentage points. Selecting the candidate with the largest positive evaluation gain accepts 13.0 changes per search, produces 75 false promotions in total, and finishes at an improvement of 7.04±0.08 points. The ± values are standard errors. A false promotion is a change with non-positive improvement on H. [Table 1](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.33180v2)

Similar final scores therefore need not imply equally reliable intermediate updates. The more conservative Bonferroni-style baseline also records zero false promotions, but its final improvement in this condition is only 2.35±0.37 points. REUSE is not the only method with zero observed errors, and the paper's SICA-style and DGM-style configuration searches are not full reproductions of those original systems. The 50,000-example H is still finite, so experimental 'true improvement' is an estimate. This evidence also does not establish independent replication by an outside team.

sections.heading: The final statistical test cannot receive all the credit
paragraphs: The appendix also discloses development-draft updates and submission screening specific to REUSE, along with removal of previously evaluated duplicate configurations. Other methods receive different information and do not use exactly the same search process. The main table consequently compares combined pipelines. Development-search rounds should also not be equated directly with formal queries to the evaluation set. [Appendix B, Tables 2–3 and 6](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.33180v2)

A test-removal experiment gives more direct evidence. The authors shrink development data to 500 examples and relax screening over ten fresh seeds, making mistaken selection easier. With the evaluation test retained, nine candidates with non-positive improvement on H are rejected, and none of 47 accepted changes is false. Without the test, six false promotions occur in five of the ten runs. Final performance does not differ significantly. This supports the test's role in update reliability, but does not establish the same effect for open-ended code changes or long-horizon agents. [Appendix B.4.1, Figure 4](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.33180v2)

sections.heading: Questions to carry into today's main reading
paragraphs: **The following are reading and engineering suggestions.** For a system that revises programs, writes memory, or changes a training pipeline, first trace evaluation feedback: who sees scores, who uses them to propose the next version, and whether final audit data returns to debugging. Development data may guide repeated exploration. But keeping another set's questions out of the agent's visible context does not make repeated queries to that set independent validation. For example, AIDE² exposes selection grades to its outer loop. It does not directly satisfy REUSE's decision-only feedback restriction, so this guarantee cannot be applied retroactively to the main paper.

Read the assumptions in Section 2.1, Algorithm 1, and Table 1 first, then Appendix B's information table and ablation; leave the statistical derivations until implementation requires them. Paired with AIDE², the value is connecting the ability to propose useful changes with a credible process for deciding which changes to retain. REUSE supplies a conditional evaluation framework; it has not empirically established sustained self-improvement in general research agents. [Full v2](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.33180v2)
